title: Brake and Clutch Systems: Fluid and Dust Precautions
introduction:
I think of the hydraulic system as having a strict guest list: only clean brake fluid meeting the manufacturer's specification belongs inside, and previously drained fluid gets no return invitation. Friction dust needs a different kind of housekeeping—making a component look clean must not mean putting its dust into the air.

I use these precautions before brake or clutch work. This page explains fluid cleanliness, friction-dust hazards and the immediate response to a paintwork spill. It is a safety overview, not a servicing procedure: the applicable fluid specification and government-approved dust-removal techniques must be established separately before carrying out that work.

items.name: Suitable brake fluid
items.detail: Use only clean brake fluid meeting the manufacturer's specification. Do not reuse previously drained fluid.

items.name: Dust-removal method
items.detail: Use government-approved techniques to remove friction dust. Do not use compressed air to blow dust from storage containers or friction components.

edits.text: WARNING: Use only clean brake fluid that meets the manufacturer's specification. Do not use any other fluid, and never reuse brake fluid that has previously been drained. These precautions help prevent system contamination, damage to brake components and the risk of serious personal injury.
edits.why: Fluid cleanliness and the correct specification protect the hydraulic system; previously drained fluid is excluded even if it appears clean.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not breathe friction-component dust. Do not use compressed air to blow dust from storage containers or friction components; remove it using government-approved techniques. Dust created while repairing friction components, such as brake pads and clutch discs, can expose you to potentially hazardous components. Friction-component dust may present a cancer and lung-disease hazard. Exposure may also irritate the skin, eyes and respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions and/or lead to other chronic health effects. If irritation persists, seek medical attention or advice. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Brake pads provide the friction material pressed against the brake disc. Dust generated during work on friction components needs controlled removal: blowing it away can create an inhalation exposure rather than resolve the hazard.

edits.text: NOTICE: If brake fluid spills onto paintwork, immediately wash the affected area down with cold water.
edits.why: Treat a paintwork spill as an immediate cleanup task; do not leave it until the brake or clutch work is finished.
